data.text:
Pure recklessness and bravado

A British man was vacationing in the Philippines. On the beach, he found a “cute little octopus,” picked it up, and calmly filmed a video.

He didn’t realize that he was holding a blue-ringed octopus — one of the most venomous creatures on the planet.

Its venom causes muscle paralysis and respiratory failure. It is about 1,000 times more toxic than cyanide, and there is no antidote.

One bite — and a person can die within minutes.

The realization came later, when commenters began flooding in, telling him he had been holding near-certain death in his hands.

data.text:
Bilang tugon sa natatalang pagtaas ng mga kaso ng aksidente tuwing holiday season — mula road crashes, emergency cases na may kinalaman sa high blood pressure, high blood sugar, at stroke, hanggang firecrackers-related injury, ginanap ang programang Ligtas Christmas 2025 noong Disyembre 12, 2025 sa Malinta National High School na pinangunahan ng Department of Health – Metro Manila Center for Health and Development (DOHMMCHD) at pakikiisa ng Valenzuela City Health Office. 

Layunin ng programang ito na paigtingin ang wiser, healthier, at safer choices ng publiko ngayong
paparating ang Pasko at Bagong Taon sa pamamagitan ng tatlong mahalagang paalala:

✅ Tamang Pagkain, Ehersisyo, at Disiplina – Pagkaroon ng balanseng nutrisyon, pag-iwas sa labis na
pag-inom ng alak at paninigarilyo, at pag-eehersisyo.
✅ BiyaHealthy – Ligtas na pagmamaneho at pagiging responsableng pedestrian.
✅ Iwas Paputok – Pag-iwas sa paggamit ng mga ipinagbabawal na paputok at paggamit ng mga ligtas
na alternatibong pampaingay at pampailaw.

Ito ay dinaluhan ng mga mag-aaral, magulang, at guro ng Malinta National High School kasama ang iba’t-ibang ahensya bilang suporta sa adbokasiya. Kabilang sa mga dumalo ay sina Dr. Lester Tan, Regional Director ng DOH-MMCHD, Dr. Janice Kathleen Malesido, Chief ng Health Program Support Division ng DOH-MMCHD, Dr. Manuel Mapue II, DMO V mula sa Health System Support and Coordination Division, at Ms. Glizelle Bercasio, DMO.

Sajid Akram, who was killed during an exchange of fire with police, had been traveling internationally on an Indian passport. Immigration officials confirm that he had also visited the Philippines shortly before the attack using the same passport.

Australian authorities have stated that Sajid Akram was a resident of Hyderabad, #India.
